doc.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Films about jazz
summary: He dislikes Lady Sings the Blues and Young Man with a Horn and finds Round Midnight okay.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Are there any films that dealt with jazz in a way that didn’t disgust you? Popular films?
Certainly not Lady Sings the Blues.

One of the films that did a disservice unintentionally was a film version of a novel called Young Man with a Horn, which propagated the view that all a jazz person had to do was get up and blow his horn. There was no history, no background, no training, nothing like that. I saw the film – what was it? – Round about Midnight, which is okay, but . . .
It’s still kind of corny, isn’t it, in a way?
I thought it was still corny, in a way. That’s my opinion, not yours.

Yeah, that’s it. I haven’t – it’s amazing. There are so many writers who have been moved by jazz, and people in the film industry, there must be some among them. But we’ve not had a novel – film, or even a novel about jazz, let along a film, that tells the story. It’s something you might consider.
